title: Kingdom of Dahomey founded
description: Fon kings based at Abomey found the Kingdom of Dahomey, which grows into the dominant state of the Slave Coast.

title: Dahomey conquers Allada
description: King Agaja takes Allada, the state from which Dahomey's dynasty had come and the region's main slave-trading port at the time.

title: Dahomey conquers Whydah
description: Agaja seizes the port of Whydah, giving Dahomey direct control of West Africa's busiest slave-exporting coast.

title: Dahomey pays tribute to Oyo
description: After invasions by the Oyo Empire's cavalry, Dahomey agrees to pay it an annual tribute, which continues into the early nineteenth century.

title: Ghezo becomes king of Dahomey
description: Ghezo overthrows his brother Adandozan with the help of the Brazilian slave trader Francisco Félix de Sousa and begins a forty-year reign.

title: First Franco-Dahomean War
description: King Béhanzin's army attacks the French position at Cotonou over a border dispute, and the war ends with a treaty that fails to settle it.

title: French take Abomey
description: Colonel Alfred Dodds' column enters the royal capital during the second war, and Béhanzin flees after firing its palaces.

title: Béhanzin surrenders
description: The last independent king of Dahomey gives himself up to the French and is exiled, first to Martinique and later to Algeria.

title: French Dahomey established
description: France organises the conquered kingdom and the coast as the colony of Dahomey and Dependencies, later part of French West Africa.

title: Dahomey becomes an overseas territory
description: Under the Fourth Republic Dahomey gets its own territorial assembly and representation in France, opening mass politics in the colony.

title: Republic of Dahomey proclaimed
description: After voting to join the French Community, the territory becomes a self-governing republic with a government under Hubert Maga.

title: Independence from France
description: The Republic of Dahomey becomes fully independent with Hubert Maga as its first president.

title: Magas government overthrown
description: Army chief Christophe Soglo deposes President Maga after street protests, the first of Dahomey's recurring military coups.

title: Kérékou seizes power
description: Major Mathieu Kérékou overthrows a rotating three-man presidential council and installs a military government.

title: People's Republic of Benin declared
description: Kérékou names the country Benin, after the ancient kingdom far to the east, and adopts Marxism-Leninism as the state ideology.

title: Operation Shrimp
description: French-led mercenaries under Bob Denard land at Cotonou airport in an attempt to overthrow Kérékou and are beaten off.

title: National Conference meets
description: A conference of representative groups declares itself sovereign, strips Kérékou of most power and opens the way to multiparty rule.

title: Republic of Benin restored
description: Marxism-Leninism is dropped and the country is renamed the Republic of Benin with a transitional government under Nicéphore Soglo.

title: Nicéphore Soglo elected president
description: Soglo defeats Kérékou in the run-off of Benin's first democratic presidential election, and the incumbent steps down.

title: Yayi Boni elected president
description: Kérékou, barred by an age limit, retires after ruling for 29 of the previous 34 years, and the banker Yayi Boni wins the election.

title: Patrice Talon elected president
description: The cotton magnate Patrice Talon wins the run-off against Prime Minister Lionel Zinsou.

title: Contested parliamentary election
description: With the opposition barred from running, elections are boycotted by much of the country and protests in Cotonou are put down by force.
